reason: E3 directly supports the formation of mixed liquid droplets and kinetic trapping under ~55 ms shocks, but the cited evidence does not experimentally demonstrate the predicted effect of systematically extending dwell time on segregation, nor does it confirm the mechanism for noble metal systems specifically.
premises: Rapid high-temperature decomposition of mixed metal salt precursors forms uniformly mixed molten droplets
Extremely short high-temperature dwell time limits atomic diffusion, preventing segregation
Rapid quenching of the mixed molten droplets locks in a single-phase solid solution
Extending the high-temperature dwell time allows atomic diffusion, leading to elemental segregation and phase separation
The mechanism is general for noble metal HEA nanoparticles under non-equilibrium flash heating conditions
